identity: Silverleaf tends its saplings for centuries; a band of confused poachers is cutting them for this week.

quests.title: A Century Down the Snout
quests.text: We planted those saplings for children yet unborn; the Small Boars consider them breakfast. Cull eight by day {dir_of:silverleaf:home_glades}; their yellow names mean they will leave you alone until you strike. Look at the cut stems while you are there, too. A snout leaves a mess, but those cuts are clean.
quests.lesson: Yellow names are neutral single pulls.

quests.title: Begin with the Grain
quests.text: Before you tend a forest, learn what a piece of wood will bear. Make one Wooden Axe and one Wooden Pickaxe and bring them to me here in Silverleaf. Your work will serve the seed store; in exchange, you shall have a tested pair from mine.
quests.lesson: Basic tools; handed-in tools are consumed, the reward replaces them.

quests.title: The Oven Keeps No Seasons
quests.text: An elf may spend a century choosing a tree; supper allows me rather less. Bring me five logs of any tree, cut outside Silverleaf's protected ground. Whole logs, please, not planks: I have an oven to feed, not a floor to mend.
quests.lesson: Any log counts, planks do not; town plants cannot be gathered.

quests.title: The Ferns Have Teeth
quests.text: Listen beneath the ferns after dark: that scratching is no woodland lullaby. Kill eight Large Rats in the glades {dir_of:silverleaf:home_glades}, before they gnaw through another season's planting. Draw them out carefully; one frightened squeal brings the neighbours.
quests.lesson: The night clock in the same area; rats call nearby rats.

quests.title: A Lesson That Holds Its Edge
quests.text: You have learned the grain; now learn the weight. Mine plain stone outside Silverleaf with your wooden pick, then make one Stone Axe and one Stone Pickaxe. Bring both here for a tested pair in exchange, and let patience guide your hands before strength does.
quests.lesson: Tool progression; rock asks for a pick tier.

quests.title: Embers Before Eloquence
quests.text: The elder can warm a gathering with a speech; I have tried it on the oven without success. Mine five Coal Lumps from the rock outside Silverleaf and bring them to me. When you cook for yourself, put fuel in the fuel slot and raw food in the cooking slot; neither benefits from a speech.
quests.lesson: Gather while waiting for night; the public oven is in town.

quests.title: The Basket-Mender's Due
quests.text: Three generations of careful weaving, and a rat decides my seed baskets need doors. Hunt Large Rats after dark in the glades {dir_of:silverleaf:home_glades} and bring me two Rat Fur Patches. I shall mend the baskets; you may keep any extra patches for your own work.
quests.lesson: Ordinary loot from an earlier hunt.

quests.title: Let the Grass Remember Footsteps
quests.text: Dune grass bends beneath a living foot and rises after it; the dead give it no such respite. Lay six Braindead Zombies to rest on the {name:strand} {zone_area:strand} at night. Go before sunrise, when the light takes them, and leave the shore its quiet.
quests.lesson: Zombies walk at night and burn in the sun.

quests.title: A Shore Supper
quests.text: Even an ancient recipe needs someone willing to get their boots wet. Bring me two Crab Legs from the Small Crabs on the {name:strand} {zone_area:strand} by day. Their yellow names mean they will not attack first. Keep any Crab Eyes for an enchanter; I prefer supper to stop watching me.
quests.lesson: The same shore by day and by night holds different mobs.

quests.title: Enough for the Latecomers
quests.text: The planting crews eat last and pretend they are not hungry. Bring me ten pieces of Raw Meat from your hunts; boars or rats will do, and anything already in your pack counts. I mean to have supper waiting before anyone has to pretend.
quests.lesson: Earlier hunt loot is useful; cooking closes the kitchen line.

quests.title: Eight Shadows in the Seedbeds
quests.text: Every spring we sow for a forest; every spring the foxes discover our generosity. Cull eight Young Foxes by day in the {name:foxglades} {zone_area:foxglades}. Mind the Aggressive Boars nearby: a red name means the creature may start the fight itself.
quests.lesson: Neutral and aggressive mobs side by side.

quests.title: A Hall Should Not Creak
quests.text: Our hall has heard a great deal of wisdom; lately its hinges insist on answering. Smelt three Copper Bars and three Tin Bars from ore around Silverleaf and bring them here for the repairs. I will give you my old Dual Furnace for your next lesson; set it up outside protected ground.
quests.lesson: Ore to bar; a portable furnace.

quests.title: Dust Is Not a Seasoning
quests.text: A little age improves a recipe, but it does nothing for the dust above my flour. Bring me two Fox Tails from Young Foxes in the {name:foxglades} {zone_area:foxglades} by day. One brush for the shelf, one held in reserve: that is how a kitchen survives an elf's idea of a short visit.
quests.lesson: A regional drop with an ordinary use.

quests.title: The Third Metal
quests.text: Copper and tin each have their virtues; put them together and you gain another. Use your Dual Furnace to alloy three Bronze Bars and bring them here, gathering fresh materials because the earlier bars went into our hinges. A Bronze Pickaxe awaits you in exchange, for the rock beyond these glades has lessons of its own.
quests.lesson: Alloys; the Bronze Pickaxe is the onward tool.

quests.title: A Forest Is Not a Woodpile
quests.text: Those clean cuts lead to the {name:poacher_camp} {dir_from_giver:poacher_camp}, occupied day and night by Confused Poachers and Confused Wood Thieves. Defeat seven of them in all, then their leader, {name:misguided_poacher_chief}; draw him apart from his guards if you can. He sees a week's firewood where we planted a century of shade.
quests.lesson: A camp and its normal-tier leader; pull the leader alone.

quests.title: Beyond the First Ring
quests.text: Twig did not teach himself to turn our trees into profit. Follow the road to Starbough Village and tell Ilyra Mossveil what happened here; the cutters in her vale have had longer to practise. Attend to any unfinished business before you leave, and remember that a forest grows one ring at a time.
quests.lesson: Start to home handoff; leave at level 10.
